Where it began

Devon Conway was born in Johannesburg on 8 July 1991, and his first cricket was played in South Africa. In 2015 he turned out for Gauteng in the Africa T20 Cup.

Then in August 2017, aged 26, he packed up and moved to New Zealand to give cricket a proper go. It was a brave step for a man in his mid-twenties, and it worked out rather well.

The player

With Wellington he soon became one of the heaviest scorers in the country. In the 2019–20 season he topped the run lists in all three domestic competitions. Along the way he made an unbeaten 327 against Canterbury and scored 393 runs in that one match, more than anyone before him had managed in one first-class game on New Zealand soil. He was twice named the country's men's domestic player of the year.

His Test career began at Lord's in June 2021, and he made 200. No man had scored more on Test debut in England, and at 29 years and 329 days he was the oldest to reach a double hundred in his first Test. A few weeks later he made 54 in the first innings as New Zealand won the World Test Championship final. By November 2026 he had played 36 Tests and made 2,761 runs at 42.48, with eight hundreds and a best of 227.

What made him special

Conway came to Test cricket later than most, nearly thirty by the time of his debut, and he wasted no time making up for it. In December 2022 he became the fastest New Zealander to 1,000 Test runs, needing only 19 innings.

He could change gears, too. In the Super Smash he once made a hundred from 49 balls, and in white-ball cricket he opened with plenty of freedom. For a man who moved countries to give his cricket a chance, he made the most of it.

Away from the middle

Wisden named him one of its five Cricketers of the Year in April 2022, and the ICC picked him as its best men's player for June 2021. In franchise cricket he played for Chennai Super Kings from 2022. In the 2023 IPL final against Gujarat Titans he made 47 from 25 balls in the chase and was named player of the match as Chennai took the title. That season he scored 672 runs, the third most in the tournament. He also played in the first season of Major League Cricket, for Texas Super Kings.

And finally

Plenty of cricketers dream of a hundred at Lord's. Conway is one of the few who did it on his first visit as a Test player, and then simply kept going until he reached 200. It was quite a way to introduce himself.
